card.band: 4 h. A frontier agent improves the baseline by tuning but with diminishing returns, and the weaker model improves little. The bucket is the normalised gain.
card.cheat: Training on the evaluation text or memorising it. The sealed corpus is absent from the image, and the model size is capped.
card.grading: Bits per character on a sealed corpus from other authors and periods, normalised between the shipped baseline loss and the reference. A random split is not used. A hard gate requires the byte-level computation to be consistent.
card.reference: Written by us: a tuned configuration with the same code under the same budget. The headroom is limited at this scale, so the reference score is measured at build.
card.source: https://github.com/karpathy/nanoGPT (data/shakespeare_char) @ 3adf61e, MIT. Data provenance is not found, so the corpus must be swapped for public-domain texts.
card.task: /app ships the nanoGPT CPU config and a public-domain multi-author character corpus for training. The agent has a fixed wall-clock budget on 8 cores to improve the model, optimiser, schedule and data handling, and delivers a checkpoint and a sampling script.
card.title: Character LM under a fixed CPU budget on unseen-author text

source_notes: Data: train.bin 1,003,854 tokens, val.bin 111,540 (readme). OOD: hold out different author/period or different genre (e.g. public-domain novels the grader holds), not a random 10 percent split. INFERRED run time: ~3 min for the 2000-iter CPU config (page; core count not stated), eval 20 iters seconds; a 30-60 min budget on 8 CPUs allows ~6-10x more compute. Overlap: none with the public corpus; risk that tiny-scale tuning saturates quickly (limited headroom 1.88 to ~1.5). Levers: model width/depth, block size, optimizer, LR schedule, dropout, tokenization (char vs small BPE), batch size.
source_version: Baseline: shipped nanoGPT CPU config; q:"This still runs in about ~3 minutes, but gets us a loss of only 1.88" (4 layers, 4 heads, 128-d, block 64, 2000 iters) -> Reference: same code with better hyperparameters / model within a wall-clock budget; page GPU run: q:"the best validation loss is 1.4697"

facts.claim: karpathy/nanoGPT exists at commit 3adf61e154c3fe3fca428ad6bc3818b27a3b8291 and contains data/shakespeare_char
data/shakespeare_char readme states train.bin has 1,003,854 tokens and val.bin has 111,540 tokens; source is Tiny Shakespeare (char-rnn)
Repository licence is MIT, copyright Andrej Karpathy (2022)
The shipped shakespeare_char config is a CPU config (seed says ~2000-iter CPU config)
Shipped config is max_iters 5000, n_layer 6, n_head 6, n_embd 384, block_size 256, dropout 0.2, lr 1e-3; device is commented out (CPU only suggested as a MacBook comment)
A public named task 'Budget NanoGPT Speedrun [METR]' exists as listed in l0_neighbours

METR's expenditure-horizon work uses the NanoGPT speedrun; GPT-5.5 and Opus-4.8 verified about 1% and 1.5% gains; GPT-5 and Opus-4.1 showed no real progress (article dated 2026-07-27, no METR report link)

full_card.band: 4 h tier. Frontier agents would tune width, depth, LR, dropout and batch with diminishing returns; weaker model improves little. Public evidence (July 2026, secondary) shows frontier agents at ~1-1.5% verified gains on the NanoGPT speedrun, which is a different metric from bpc.
full_card.build_cost: 2 days or less: install CPU torch, run prepare.py, select and clean public-domain corpora, write the grader and normalisation. Smoke build verdict none is expected: the repo has no test suite and the run_rcs of 1 come from the placeholder cmd_test 'false', not from a training failure.
full_card.deliverable: Checkpoint plus sampling script; scored as bits per character on a sealed held-out author/period corpus, normalised between the shipped baseline loss and the reference.
full_card.gates_anticheat: Held-out corpus absent from image and grader-only; model size cap; byte-level consistency gate. Hyperparameter tuning cannot memorise an unseen corpus, so the main cheat is leaking held-out text into the training set, which is closable by sealing.
full_card.grading_surface: One or a few held-out texts yielding one bpc number per run; not thousands of cases. Could be widened to several authors, but the seed does not specify it.
full_card.local_fit: CPU-only, 8 cores, 16 GB: a ~10M parameter char model is trainable on CPU. Fits the sandbox.
full_card.lookup: partial. The tinyshakespeare config is public and recallable, but the sealed corpus and its tuned values are not. Frontier models know nanoGPT defaults, so the baseline is not a secret.
full_card.provenance: karpathy/nanoGPT @ 3adf61e (MIT, verified). Data folder shakespeare_char has no provenance statement; corpus must be replaced with public-domain multi-author texts, none selected yet.
full_card.reference: Our own tuned config on the same code and budget; not an independent implementation; score measured only at build; headroom ~1.88 to ~1.5 bpc (seed estimate, unverified).
full_card.ships: nanoGPT code and shakespeare_char-style config (the shipped config is not CPU-targeted; device is commented out), a public-domain training corpus, and a held-out OOD split kept by the grader.
full_card.similarity: S-rs-001 (0.418, internal seed, not a public task). METR speedrun (0.236) and RE-Bench nanoGPT chat RL (0.102) are different deliverables. Not a K1 near-duplicate, but close to the same family of nanoGPT tuning.

v1.kill_reason: One lever in practice: the score moves mainly through hyperparameter tuning of one ~10M-parameter character model, with a seeded headroom of ~0.4 bpc and the seed itself predicting diminishing returns and a weak weaker-model result. The multiple listed levers (width, block, optimiser, schedule, dropout, tokenisation, batch) are all knobs on one config, so they give neither multi-part scope nor a long chain of dependent work. The 4 h tier is therefore not justified, and the normalised bpc gives little beyond a single number.

Band.why: Seed predicts diminishing returns and frontier gains near 1-1.5% on the related speedrun; no evidence a frontier agent reaches 0.9 of the reference in some trials.

Build.why: About 2 days: CPU torch install, corpus curation, grader and normalisation.

Fit.why: CPU 8 cores 16 GB fits a small char model; a 4 h run is feasible.

Hor.why: 4 h is enough for tuning; work is repetitive sweeps rather than long dependent engineering.

Lic.why: Repo is MIT (verified); the new public-domain corpus still needs its licence checked.

Multi.why: Levers are knobs on one config collapsing to one scalar; partial credit is weak.

Nov.why: No public task neighbour above 0.42 (internal seed at 0.418); METR speedrun differs in deliverable and metric.

Real.why: nanoGPT real, MIT, commit exists; the corpus is not yet chosen and the CPU config claim is contradicted.

Ref.why: Reference is our own tuned config on the same code, not an independent implementation; headroom is small and unmeasured.

Seal.why: Held-out corpus can be kept out of the image and the grader can hold it, but the public-domain selection needs care.

Surf.why: Grader is one or a few held-out texts giving one bpc number per run; no thousands of cases.

spike_plan.kill_if: Sweep gain is within seed variance, or total achievable gain on the held-out author is under about 0.1 bpc (confirms K10: one-lever, no headroom to fill 4 h).
spike_plan.pass_if: Best sweep config beats baseline by more than 3x the seed variance on the held-out author, and the ranking transfers to the held-out author.
steps: In a throwaway Linux container with network, clone karpathy/nanoGPT at 3adf61e and install CPU-only torch.
Run data/shakespeare_char/prepare.py and train with the shipped config at 2000 iters on 8 CPU cores; record wall-clock and val bpc.
Run 3 seeds of the baseline to measure run-to-run variance in bpc.
Sweep 4 to 6 configs (width/depth, LR, dropout, block size) at the same budget on public Shakespeare val; record the spread.
Pick two public-domain authors not in the training set and hold one out; compute bpc with the same sampler/tokeniser; check that the sweep ranking holds on the held-out author.
Check determinism: rerun the best config with a fixed seed and confirm identical bpc.

v1.summary: S-rs-002 is killed under K10: the score is driven mainly by hyperparameter tuning of one small character model, and the seed itself predicts diminishing returns and little headroom, so the 4 h tier and multi-part scope are not justified. The nanoGPT repo, MIT licence and dataset counts check out, but the shipped config is not CPU-targeted and the reference is an unmeasured tuned config.
